title: US midterm elections on 3 November: control of Congress is at stake
dek: All 435 House seats, 35 Senate seats and 36 governorships are on the ballot. Republicans hold narrow majorities in both chambers; the parties' closing pitches centre on prices.
happened: Americans vote on Tuesday, 3 November. On the ballot are all 435 seats in the House of Representatives, 35 of the 100 Senate seats (33 regular races plus special elections in Florida and Ohio), governors in 36 states and 145 statewide ballot measures, including abortion, voter ID and taxes. Republicans hold the House by 218 to 214 and the Senate by 53 to 47.

sides.says: Trump told voters: "If you elect a Republican House and a Republican Senate on Nov. 3, we will continue to put America first every single day," and said "the Democrats caused the high prices ... and we're fixing them." He called higher petrol prices from the war with Iran "a small price to pay" for security. House Speaker Mike Johnson warned of a "dark, dangerous road to communism".

House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries called Trump's record a "graveyard of broken promises" and vowed to "hold the crooks accountable". Democrats are campaigning on living costs and corruption, including Medicaid cuts, the Iran war and expiring health insurance subsidies. Texas Senate nominee James Talarico said the vote is about "whether you want a politician who puts money in your pocket or his own".

next: The first polls close at 6 p.m. Eastern (23:00 GMT) in parts of Kentucky and Indiana and the last at 1 a.m. Eastern in Alaska. Some races may take days or weeks to call. Democrats need a net gain of three House seats and four Senate seats to win control; a 50–50 Senate stays Republican because Vice President JD Vance breaks ties.
summary: The 2026 midterms decide who controls Congress for the second half of Donald Trump's term. Republicans have narrow majorities: 218 to 214 in the House and 53 to 47 in the Senate. Since 1946 the president's party has lost an average of 26.5 House seats in midterm elections. Key Senate contests include Alaska, Iowa, Maine, Michigan, Texas and Ohio. Voters list living costs, abortion, immigration, the state of democracy and the war with Iran among their issues. Results start after 23:00 GMT on 3 November, but close races may take days.
